data.narrative:
ADASI, a defense and security company acquired by EDGE Group and sovereign-funded, presents a valuation challenge typical of late-stage frontier-tech assets in its sector. The broader Defense & Security universe comprises 21 peer companies, with 2 public comparables (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private peers including Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, Saronic, and Quantum-Systems.

The peer-median triangulation method is not applicable here. Despite identifying 21 same-sector peers, the dataset contains zero companies matching ADASI's stage, zero at adjacent stages, and zero within similar valuation tiers—falling short of the three-datapoint minimum required for statistical reliability. Applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable selection bias given the heterogeneity of defense and security subsegments, their distinct risk profiles, and capital intensity variations.

This analysis therefore cannot support a specific valuation range without additional quantitative anchors. The identified peer universe—particularly Anduril, Helsing, and Shield AI—would provide meaningful comparables if stage-equivalent funding rounds, revenue multiples, or recent transactions were available. Given ADASI's sovereign funding structure and acquisition status, traditional venture-stage metrics may not apply. Future valuation work should prioritize obtaining transaction prices or recent funding terms from the top-tier private peer set to establish a defensible range.
